To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adaptation to the characteristic patterns of spatial contrast in natural scenes induces characteristic changes in spatial sensitivity, and that adaptation to local distortions in face images induces strong figural aftereffects.

(1) contrast thresholds are reduced by adaptation to stimuli that are representative of the visual environment, and (2) adaptation to natural stimuli induces figural aftereffects, which bias perception in a direction that is opposite to the adapting stimulus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of visual adaptation and how these mechanisms are shaped by the visual environment.
the mechanisms by which visual processing is adjusted to the prevailing conditions of stimulation.
the mechanisms of adaptation and their functional implications for vision.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adaptation does not seem to depend strongly on the spatial structure of the natural visual input, but rather on the statistics of the input.
adaptation is a process that occurs in all sensory systems.
the visual system is adapted to the statistics of natural stimuli, but that this adaptation is not a simple consequence of the statistics of the stimuli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

contrast adaptation is an important mechanism in the visual system that can be used to explain the effects of viewing natural images, and that it can be used to enhance performance of image processing systems.
the spatial structure of natural scenes has a strong influence on the state of adaptation, and hence the way that the visual system responds to subsequent stimuli.

the adaptation to natural images is a general process that does not depend on the specific spatial frequency spectrum of the image, but that the adaptation is selective in terms of the type of stimulus that is used for adaptation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial statistics of natural scenes are important in determining how the visual system responds to them.
the natural environment has a strong effect on visual processing.
contrast adaptation can have a strong effect on the way we see the world around us.
